title: Vendor onboarding: MSA/DPA exceptions + SLA/pricing approval
summary: Kickoff to drive vendor acceptance: discuss MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers for dedicated vs hosted, pricing approval path, KMS/egress constraints and data residency. Agreed to follow-up with security package and draft pricing sheet; procurement to run legal redline in 1 week.
topics: KMS / key custody and egress fees

Procurement/legal to consolidate redlines and schedule negotiation call w/ legal next Friday
SE to run a short perf benchmark if customer wants a dedicated-peak comparison
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-16
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Nathan Reyes (Palmetto Procurement), Aisha Khan (Palmetto Legal), Derek Lee (Platform Lead), Sonia Varela (Cloud Security)

Auto-generated summary:
Redwood and Palmetto initial onboarding and contract kickoff. Primary blockers: DPA redline around data usage & subproces-sors, SLA p99 latency targets for high-throughput use, KMS / key custody expectations, and a procurement approval window that needs pricing clarity.

[00:00] Maria Chen: Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maria, I'm the AE on this account, and Jordan our SE is here to walk through the technical and SLA questions. How are you all?
[00:12] Nathan Reyes: Hey, good thanks. We're keen to, uh, get this moving, procurement timeline is tight — approval needed by end of month ideally.
[00:20] Aisha Khan: Hi all. From legal side we have a couple DPA exceptions we need to flag, mostly around subprocessors and data retention.
[00:28] Jordan Patel: Hi everyone. Quick note, I may jump in on the SLA and performance comments, and also on the dedicated/private deployment options.
[00:36] Derek Lee: Quick context — Palmetto will use the inference service for customer-facing document summarization and alerts, so p99 latency during market hours is a hard constraint.
[00:45] Sonia Varela: And from security we need to confirm key management — we prefer bring-your-own-key or customer-managed KMS, and also audit log retention for 7 years, that's a statutory ask in our line of business.
[00:58] Maria Chen: Totally understood. I'll flag that for the MSA/DPA conversation. On KMS we do have a private deployment option with customer-managed keying — Jordan can explain details.
[01:12] Jordan Patel: Yeah. So high level: Redwood offers hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem. For BYOK we provide integrations with cloud KMS providers and an on-prem HSM path for Private. There are some differences in egress handling and logging depending on mode.
[01:30] Aisha Khan: Regarding the DPA, one of the sticking points is subprocessor notice and the ability to object. We do need a formal notice window and a carveout for certain jurisdictions. Also retention — can we limit retention to 30 days except where required by law?
[01:47] Maria Chen: Those are reasonable asks. Our standard DPA has a 90-day retention default but we can propose a 30-day configuration for enterprise accounts and a clause for law enforcement exceptions. I'll flag that as a redline.
[01:58] Nathan Reyes: From procurement — pricing clarity is the blocker; we need a worksheet to show committed monthly spend vs overage and the SLA credit mechanics. Also what happens if we breach the p99 SLA? The procurement committee wants numeric credits, not just vague language.
[02:15] Jordan Patel: For SLAs we usually have tiered credits: for dedicated we can commit to a tighter p99 and smaller credits, for hosted there is a different scale. I can sketch a 3-tier SLA matrix: hosted, dedicated, private — with p50/p95/p99 targets and credit percentages.
[02:33] Aisha Khan: Also we need to confirm whether logs and transcripts of requests are considered customer data or service metadata; that affects the DPA language about processing purposes.
[02:42] Maria Chen: In our model, request/response content is customer data; telemetry and anonymized metrics are service data. But I acknowledge the wording can be tightened. We'll propose explicit definitions.
[02:53] Derek Lee: On the performance side — can Jordan give some ballpark latencies for a 2k token summarization workload? We need to map to our SLOs during market hours.
[03:03] Jordan Patel: Sure — on dedicated A100-like hardware, 2k tokens with our default model variants is around 150-250ms per token on average though that can vary. For end-to-end latency we look at prefix behavior — usually 300-600ms for many requests but depends on batching and KV cache. Sorry that's a bit fuzzy, but I can put a clearer bench with numbers.
[03:25] Nathan Reyes: Those per-token numbers mean a lot. Procurement will want a comparison: dedicated vs hosted cost per 1M tokens and how autoscaling impacts price.
[03:34] Maria Chen: We'll include a pricing worksheet that models committed vs burst costs. Note that private deployments typically have different licensing — we'll call that out.
[03:41] Sonia Varela: On KMS — BYOK is a hard requirement. We also mandate that Redwood not hold plaintext keys and we need an attestation or design doc showing keyflow.
[03:50] Jordan Patel: Right — for Private we can do a customer KMS where the key never leaves the customer's control; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in the cloud provider. We'll share architecture diagrams.
[04:03] Aisha Khan: Can we get a copy of your SOC2 and any pen test reports? Also we need to see audit log granularity: who accessed what, request IDs, timestamps.
[04:12] Maria Chen: Absolutely. I'll push the security pack with SOC2 report and a summarized pen-test outcome. Audit log schema will be in the package.
[04:20] Derek Lee: One more technical Q — how do you handle KV cache invalidation during model rollouts? We don't want cache staleness causing inconsistent outputs.
[04:30] Jordan Patel: Good question. We version KV caches by model build and have deterministic invalidation on rollout; for canaries we keep separate cache namespaces so older inferences don't pollute new serving paths. Sorry, bit of ops-speak there.
[04:50] Nathan Reyes: Back to procurement — timeline. We need pricing and DPA redlines back to us by next Friday to make the internal committee the following week. Is that realistic?
[04:59] Maria Chen: Yes. Jordan and I will get the SLA matrix + pricing worksheet out by Monday, and the security pack today. Aisha, you'll take the DPA redline and send comments by Friday?
[05:10] Aisha Khan: We'll try. Legal will need to coordinate with privacy counsel, but Friday is our target.
[05:18] Maria Chen: Great. Any major objections on the pricing approach being credits vs termination rights? I know some customers ask for termination; typically we offer credit ladders and for severe SLA failures termination clauses are evaluated case-by-case.
[05:31] Derek Lee: Credits are OK as long as there's a clear formula and they're meaningful. Termination is a nuclear option, procurement won't push it unless severe.
[05:39] Sonia Varela: On data residency — some subsets of customer PII must remain in EU. Can Redwood partition workloads regionally?
[05:47] Jordan Patel: Yes, we have region-aware routing policies and can pin model serving to regions for residency. For private deployments you get full control.
[05:56] Nathan Reyes: One small but important item — egress fees. If we export logs or if we pull heavy replays for debugging, who bears egress costs? Procurement wants clarity.
[06:06] Maria Chen: Good call. We typically outline egress responsibilities in the pricing appendix: customer pays cloud-provider egress for data pulled out of their region, but we can scope debug exports in the SOW. We'll make that explicit.
[06:18] Aisha Khan: Also request a clause on indemnities related to model outputs — we need to limit liability tied to downstream consumer actions.
[06:26] Maria Chen: Understood. We'll share our standard indemnity language; if you have specific requirements please flag them.
[06:33] Jordan Patel: I'll follow up with a short technical appendix covering KMS flows, KV cache, and how rollouts work — that'll help legal and security teams understand risk surface.
[06:45] Nathan Reyes: Ok, so to recap — Redwood shares security pack now, SLA & pricing spreadsheet by Monday, Palmetto legal to return DPA redlines by Friday, and then we'll schedule a redline negotiation next Friday. Procurement to confirm internal committee date.
[07:00] Maria Chen: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:05] Derek Lee: Maybe a short POC for a dedicated perf run once we have a pricing outline. That will help make the decision.
[07:12] Jordan Patel: We can set up a 2-hour dedicated bench with representative load — can do that as a paid pilot or scoped POC.
[07:20] Maria Chen: Great — I'll include POC options in the pricing worksheet. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and upload artifacts.
[07:28] Aisha Khan: Thanks.
[07:30] Nathan Reyes: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
